 By Daily Camera letters | openforum@dailycamera.com | Boulder Daily Camera PUBLISHED: October 31, 2026 at 4:00 AM MDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Ryan Schuchard and Tina Marquis are on the right path
 Ryan Schuchard and Tina Marquis have served on Boulder City Council for three years, and they have spent them on the city’s hardest problems. With their colleagues, they’ve worked on expanding housing options, sustainably funding pothole repairs and other street maintenance, reducing homelessness, increasing safety and implementing real action on wildfire resilience. They’ve begun to tackle problems that the city has deferred for decades.
 Recognizing the need to modernize the city’s long-term strategy, Ryan and Tina have begun championing greater transparency, stronger oversight, and structural improvements to how Boulder manages its budget and capital project expenditures. In doing so, they are working alongside their council colleagues to tackle a budget burden inherited from past administrations.
 As far back as 2011, the Daily Camera reported a capital maintenance backlog in the hundreds of millions of dollars, and quoted the former city manager saying, “It’s not our responsibility today to reduce a funding gap that’s going to occur 20 years from now.” We’ve since elected many new leaders. It would have been easy for our current council to again leave it for the next council. Instead, this council acknowledged the problem and put a proposed solution in front of voters. Whatever you think of the bond, the problem was not hidden — this council made a decision to increase transparency and stop deferring it.
 In its October 4 endorsement , the Daily Camera said our city council incumbents have “continued Boulder on the path of steady progress.” I agree.
 I hope you will join me in voting to keep Ryan Schuchard and Tina Marquis on our city council.
 Lisa Snow, Boulder 
 Don’t forget Biden’s student loan forgiveness
 I agree: Trump is trying to buy votes. But let’s not forget Biden’s student loan forgiveness.
 Ken Staroscik, Firestone 
 Start over on passenger rail vote
 Thousands of voters who live outside the Front Range Passenger Rail district got ballots erroneously including the rail sales tax issue. Now county clerks are trying to omit all of the votes on those ballots, and without counting any votes that shouldn’t be included. It seems the only way to have a truly valid vote is to throw out the results from this election and have another vote with the correct district borders.
 Robert Ito, Boulder
